mcqs.learning_point: Understand historical development of cell theory
mcqs.question: Which of the following comparisons correctly describes the contributions of Schleiden and Schwann to the development of cell theory?

options.A: Schleiden proposed that all plants are composed of cells, while Schwann proposed that all animals are composed of cells.
options.B: Schleiden discovered cells using a microscope, whereas Schwann disproved the cell theory.
options.C: Both Schleiden and Schwann argued that cells arise spontaneously from non‑living matter.
options.D: Schleiden and Schwann suggested that cells are the smallest unit of life but denied that all organisms are made of cells.

mcqs.answer: Schleiden proposed that all plants are composed of cells, while Schwann proposed that all animals are composed of cells.
mcqs.explanation: Schleiden (1838) stated that all plant tissues are made of cells, and Schwann (1839) extended this to animals, forming the two core statements of the cell theory. The other options misrepresent their work or contradict the established contributions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sets of statements correctly states the cell theory as accepted in modern biology?

options.A: All living organisms are composed of one or more cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.B: All living organisms are composed of cells; cells can arise spontaneously from non‑living matter; the cell is the basic unit of life.
options.C: Only multicellular organisms are composed of cells; cells are the basic unit of structure; cells arise from non‑living matter.
options.D: All living organisms are composed of cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure; cells arise only from other cells during embryonic development.

mcqs.answer: All living organisms are composed of one or more cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
mcqs.explanation: Option A includes the three universally accepted tenets: (1) all organisms are cellular, (2) the cell is the structural and functional unit, and (3) biogenesis – cells arise only from existing cells. The other options introduce spontaneous generation or omit the functional aspect, which are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which statement best describes the difference between unicellular and multicellular organisms?

options.A: Unicellular organisms consist of a single cell that performs all life functions, whereas multicellular organisms consist of many specialized cells that work together.
options.B: Unicellular organisms have multiple cells, while multicellular organisms have a single cell.
options.C: Unicellular organisms lack a nucleus, while multicellular organisms always have a nucleus.
options.D: Unicellular organisms can only be prokaryotes, while multicellular organisms are always eukaryotes.

mcqs.answer: Unicellular organisms consist of a single cell that performs all life functions, whereas multicellular organisms consist of many specialized cells that work together.
mcqs.explanation: A unicellular organism (e.g., Amoeba) carries out all metabolic activities within one cell. Multicellular organisms (e.g., humans) have differentiated cells that specialize for tasks such as transport, protection, and signaling. The other options are factually inaccurate.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise exceptions and refinements at the required level
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an exception to the statement "All cells arise from pre‑existing cells"?

options.A: Viruses, because they replicate without cellular machinery.
options.B: Bacterial cells, because they can arise spontaneously.
options.C: Plant cells, because they develop from non‑cellular tissue.
options.D: Animal muscle cells, because they divide without parent cells.

mcqs.answer: Viruses, because they replicate without cellular machinery.
mcqs.explanation: Viruses are not cells; they reproduce by using host cellular machinery, so they do not arise from pre‑existing viruses in the same way cells do. Bacterial, plant, and animal cells all follow biogenesis, dividing from parent cells.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand historical development of cell theory
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines the cell theory and distinguishes it from the earlier concept of spontaneous generation?

options.A: Cell theory states that all living things are made of cells and that cells arise only from pre‑existing cells, rejecting spontaneous generation.
options.B: Cell theory claims that cells can arise spontaneously from non‑living matter, supporting spontaneous generation.
options.C: Cell theory suggests that only plants are composed of cells, while animals are not.
options.D: Cell theory denies that cells are the basic unit of life, focusing on tissues instead.

mcqs.answer: Cell theory states that all living things are made of cells and that cells arise only from pre‑existing cells, rejecting spontaneous generation.
mcqs.explanation: The modern cell theory, formulated by Schleiden, Schwann and later Virchow, explicitly rejects spontaneous generation and asserts biogenesis. Options B‑D misrepresent the theory.

mcqs.question: A researcher discovers a new microscopic organism. Which three statements of the cell theory are applicable to this organism?

options.A: All living organisms are composed of cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.B: All living organisms are composed of cells; cells can arise spontaneously; the cell is the basic unit of life.
options.C: Only multicellular organisms are composed of cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure; cells arise from non‑living matter.
options.D: Cells are the smallest unit of life; cells can be created de novo; cells are not the basic unit of function.

mcqs.answer: All living organisms are composed of cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
mcqs.explanation: Option A lists the three universally accepted tenets of cell theory, which apply to any newly discovered living organism. The other options introduce spontaneous generation or limit the theory to multicellular life, which are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which pair correctly matches an example organism with its cellular organization?
mcqs.explanation: Amoeba is a classic unicellular protozoan, while humans are composed of many specialized cells. The other pairs incorrectly assign the type of organization to the organisms.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise exceptions and refinements at the required level
mcqs.question: In humans, mature red blood cells lack a nucleus. Which refinement of the cell theory best explains this observation?

options.A: The cell theory acknowledges that some specialized cells may lose certain organelles during differentiation.
options.B: The cell theory states that all cells must retain a nucleus throughout their lifespan.
options.C: The cell theory claims that red blood cells are not cells because they lack a nucleus.
options.D: The cell theory suggests that red blood cells arise spontaneously from plasma.

mcqs.answer: The cell theory acknowledges that some specialized cells may lose certain organelles during differentiation.
mcqs.explanation: Modern cell theory is refined to allow that during differentiation, certain cells (e.g., mammalian erythrocytes) discard organelles like the nucleus to optimize function. Options B‑D contradict established knowledge.
